_comment: Each probe is a capability question, the file the documented route leads to, and the
pattern that proves the answer is actually there. They are deliberately brittle: a probe
that keeps passing while its subject changes certifies a route that no longer leads
Several exist because the thing they guard was measured and found broken during the
build -- the wire types vanishing behind a private module, namespace packages Griffe
cannot see, assignment aliases that never became aliases. Those are the rows most likely
to regress silently, so they get an assertion rather than a comment.

probes.question: Do the MCP wire types survive the private module they are defined in?
Is the importable spelling preferred over the defining path?
Does the two-hop alias chain for Client land on the real class?
Are namespace-package subpackages indexed rather than silently dropped?
Did anything fail to index without being recorded?
Is an importable class that is absent from __all__ still present?
Is a module-level assignment alias recorded as an alias?
Is a re-export from an unindexed distribution findable by name?
Are intended re-exports distinguished from incidental import sites?
Are all eighteen removed constructor keywords catalogued?
Does the removed-API catalog carry upstream's own replacement text?
Is a FastMCP server recorded as being itself a Provider?
Does the extension-point catalog report the transitive closure, not direct children?
Are the protocol eras enumerated rather than collapsed?
Is a conditionally defined name recorded with the branch it took?
Does the registration catalog state what the decorator actually returns?
Are inferred types marked as second-class rather than presented as declared?
Is the async obligation on Middleware hooks stated?
Does the distribution map say where FastMCP's code actually lives?
Is the vendored SDK module never offered as a usable import?
Does any symbol claim to be nameable while preferring a private path?
Which construct do I want: a Provider, a Transform, or middleware?
The capability map must lead with composition, not with an alphabetical list.
Does the composition topic actually reach the removed-API answer?
Does a topic page link into the vendored upstream prose?
What must I implement to write a Middleware, and what is already defaulted?
Does the Middleware page carry full hook signatures, not just names?
Which auth class does upstream actually subclass?
AuthProvider must be shown as having real obligations, not zero.
Where is FastMCP defined, and over what line range?
Does the location table carry members, not only top-level items?
Which optional install unlocks the Azure auth provider?
The extras table must map extras to modules, not just repeat the lockfile.
Which members are abstract, so that a subclass must supply them?
Is the removed-keyword rule generated from the data rather than typed?
Does the generated rule still carry all eighteen keywords?
Is there a worked upstream example of registering a tool?
Does the corpus carry the deployment guidance, not just the API?
Is the MCP specification text available for the current protocol era?
A dispatcher signature must still be marked, now that the flag is emitted.
The index must not offer a removed constructor keyword as current API.
The extras table must not have degraded back to bare lockfile rows.
Who calls FastMCP? The index used to say this was unanswerable.
Is import-time code named as a caller, rather than reported as a raw id?
A decorator expression is a real call site; is it named as one?
Where is Context referenced, and in how many files?
Are references into typeshed separated from references into this library?
Which parameters of FastMCP.__init__ are keyword-only, and required?
Does the parameter table carry resolved annotations, not local spellings?
What is the resolved MRO of FastMCP, as against its declared bases?
Which symbols are least typed, and where did upstream suppress?
Which items does this library use most? The triage question.
What imports what, at file level?
Where do I start for 'who calls this'?
Does the cross-reference page say a constructor call resolves to the class?
Which of 3,056 symbols will I actually meet?
How well typed is this library, and where is it weakest?
The typing page must distinguish Any from untyped, not merge them.
The import graph must not be offered as a call graph.
probes.expect: It is not a call graph

probes.question: The cross-reference page must not claim coverage outside the indexed set.
Do the two engines agree about an inferred type, and is disagreement findable?
probes.expect: \d+ agree · \d+ where ty is narrower · \d+ differ

probes.question: Which classes actually satisfy a Protocol, and what disqualifies a near miss?
Does the conformance page keep the variance caveat?
Do the older catalogs now say which of their entries matter?
Does the agreement page separate precision from conflict?
